summary: Provisional curated event-subscriber access for targeted billing reconciliation and compliance review
description:
Issue summary: Finance Ops requests timeboxed, read-only access to curated event-subscriber telemetry (message-level metadata and routing traces) to reconcile a customer billing discrepancy and verify usage attribution.

Impact: Customer invoice underpayment suspected (~$18k over two months). Finance needs targeted evidence to reconcile billing lines with ingestion events. Low risk to production if access is scoped and timeboxed correctly.

Requestor: Riley Chen (Finance Ops) via internal ticket and Slack #finance.

Justification: Cross-check event ingestion timestamps and subscriber acknowledgements for a single account (acct_9d7f). Current query tooling does not surface per-subscriber transient routing metadata needed for reconciliation; support previously suggested a scoped event-subscriber slice.

Timebox: 72 hours of access, start window earliest 2026-03-17 08:00 UTC, end 2026-03-20 08:00 UTC.

Scope (explicit):
- Only event-subscriber records with customer_account_id = acct_9d7f and event_time between 2026-01-01 and 2026-02-28.
- Fields: event_id, ingestion_time, subscriber_endpoint_id, routing_node, enqueue_latency_ms, delivery_status_code, tracing_id. No full request/response payloads.
- No free-text payloads, no session or user-generated content fields.

Data selectors / query example:
SELECT event_id, ingestion_time, subscriber_endpoint_id, routing_node, enqueue_latency_ms, delivery_status_code, tracing_id FROM subscriber_events WHERE customer_account_id = 'acct_9d7f' AND ingestion_time BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-02-28';

Security controls requested: ephemeral IAM role with least privilege, KMS-wrapped temporary S3 export with dual-control release, mandatory redaction job to strip any accidental payload fields, and all operations logged to audit-logging index.

Required approvals: Security (Data Protection), SRE (telemetry pipeline owner), Legal if any payload fields are included accidentally.

Steps to reproduce / access path: N/A — this is an access request for scoped query/export rather than a bug reproduction.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-11 - SRE initial check: subscriber_events index retains routing_node and tracing_id for 90 days in prod-us-east, retention post-90d moves to cold storage where subscriber_endpoint_id may be truncated. For Jan-Feb range we are within hot retention.
2026-03-12 - Found one outlier: a small cohort (~120 events) where delivery_status_code is NULL due to backpressure rejection; flagged for follow-up with ingestion team.
2026-03-13 - Dry-run produced ~42,300 rows matching selectors. Redaction scanner found 0 columns flagged as free-text; safe to export fields requested.

SRE hypothesis: billing discrepancy likely due to transient requeueing between routing nodes causing duplicate enqueue counts visible to billing. Export should confirm duplicate tracing_id occurrences tied to requeues.
resolution: PENDING - scheduled export for 2026-03-17 08:00 UTC. Will perform automated PII scan and dual-control release.
If export confirms duplicates, Finance to open charge-adjustment request and notify customer with supporting evidence. SRE will follow up with ingestion team to remediate requeue behavior.

Post-access checklist: (1) revoke ephemeral IAM role, (2) delete S3 artifact after confirmation and archival policy, (3) store audit trail and signed attestation in compliance folder, (4) create follow-up INT ticket for ingestion remediation if needed.
